answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates along bounded-length random-walk voyages from independently anchored sources, so adding internal attestations alone cannot amplify a Sybil cluster’s influence. If its shale-like boundary has low conductance—few weighted edges leave relative to its volume—then finite walks cross that cut infrequently. Conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds therefore constrain the cluster’s aggregate voting weight by its external connectivity, not its internal size or any single vertex.
